title: Open CMD as Administrator
desc:
Press Start, type  cmd , right-click 'Command Prompt' > Run as administrator.
Shortcut: Win+R, type cmd, then press Ctrl+Shift+Enter.
Or Win+X > Terminal (Admin).
Many repair commands (sfc, DISM, netsh reset, chkdsk...) need this.

title: Get help for any command
desc: Shows the built-in help and all options of any CMD command.
example:
dir /?
robocopy /?
help            :: list of built-in commands

title: Clear the screen
desc: Clears the CMD window.

title: Change folder (cd)
desc: Moves into another folder. Use  cd ..  to go up one level and  cd /d  to change drive too.
example:
cd C:\Users
cd ..
cd \              :: go to the root of the drive
cd /d D:\Games    :: change drive + folder
D:              :: just switch drive

title: List files in a folder (dir)
desc: Lists files and folders. Useful options: /a shows hidden files, /s includes subfolders, /b bare names only, /o sorts.
example:
dir /a              :: include hidden & system files
dir /s /b *.mp4     :: find all mp4 files in subfolders
dir /o:-s           :: sort by size, biggest first
dir /o:d            :: sort by date

title: Command history
desc: Shows commands typed in this window. Press F7 for a popup history list, Up/Down arrows to cycle, F3 repeats last command.

title: Exit CMD
desc: Closes the Command Prompt window (or ends a batch script).

title: Run a program / open a file
desc: Opens a program, file, folder or website with its default app, in a new window.
example:
start notepad
start .                     :: open current folder in Explorer
start https://google.com
start "" "C:\My Folder\file.pdf"

title: Show text / variable (echo)
desc: Prints text or a variable value.
example:
echo Hello
echo %USERNAME%
echo %PATH%
echo. > empty.txt      :: create empty file

title: Save command output to a file
desc: >  overwrites the file, >>  appends, 2>&1 also captures errors.
example:
ipconfig /all > C:\net.txt
dir >> list.txt
mycommand > log.txt 2>&1

title: Copy command output to clipboard
desc: Pipes the output into the clipboard so you can paste it anywhere.

title: Filter output (find / findstr)
desc: Shows only lines containing the text. /i = ignore case. findstr supports regular expressions.
example:
ipconfig | findstr IPv4
tasklist | findstr /i chrome
netstat -ano | findstr :80

title: Run several commands in one line
desc: &  runs both.  &&  runs the second only if the first succeeded.  ||  runs the second only if the first failed.
example:
ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew
mkdir test || echo folder already exists

title: Environment variables (set)
desc: Shows all variables. set NAME=value sets one for this window only. Use setx for permanent.
example:
set                  :: show all
set PATH
set MYVAR=hello
setx MYVAR "hello"    :: permanent (new windows)
echo %USERPROFILE% %APPDATA% %TEMP%

title: Add a folder to PATH (permanent)
desc:
Adds a folder so programs in it can be run from anywhere. Open a NEW CMD after this.
Warning: setx truncates values longer than 1024 chars. Safer: Win+R > sysdm.cpl > Advanced > Environment Variables > Path > Edit > New.

title: Where is a program? (where)
desc: Shows the full path of the program that runs when you type its name.
example:
where python
where git
where /r C:\ notepad.exe   :: search the whole drive

title: Change CMD colors / title
desc: First digit = background, second = text (0 black, A green, F white...). title changes the window title.
example:
color 0A
color 07          :: default
title My Window

title: Use UTF-8 / Arabic text in CMD
desc: Switches the console code page to UTF-8 so Arabic and special characters display better. chcp alone shows the current code page.

title: Pause / wait
desc: Waits 10 seconds (any key skips). /nobreak ignores keys. pause waits for a key.

title: Date and time
desc: Shows current date/time.  date  and  time  without /t let you change them (admin).

title: Who am I (current user)
desc: Shows current user. /priv shows privileges, /groups shows groups.

title: Create a folder
desc: Creates a folder (md does the same). Creates parent folders too.

title: Delete a file
desc: Deletes files. /f forces read-only files, /q no confirmation, /s also in subfolders. Deleted files do NOT go to the Recycle Bin.

title: Delete a folder with everything inside
desc: Deletes a folder and all its contents without asking. Cannot be undone!

title: Copy files
desc: Copies one or more files.
example:
copy file.txt D:\Backup\
copy *.jpg D:\Photos\
copy a.txt+b.txt all.txt   :: join files

title: Copy folders (xcopy)
desc: Copies folders with subfolders. /e include empty folders, /i dest is folder, /h hidden files, /y no overwrite prompt.

title: Copy / backup big folders (robocopy)
desc:
The best copy tool: resumes, retries, copies only changed files.
/e subfolders, /mir mirror (also DELETES extra files in dest!), /mt:16 multi-thread, /r:1 /w:1 fewer retries, /z restartable.
example:
robocopy "C:\Users\Me\Documents" "E:\Backup\Docs" /e /mt:16 /r:1 /w:1
robocopy C:\src D:\dst /mir      :: exact mirror

title: Move files
desc: Moves files or folders (also renames).

title: Rename a file
desc: Renames a file or folder. Wildcards work for extensions.

title: Show file contents
desc: Prints a text file in CMD. Use  more  for page by page.

title: Create a file
desc: Creates a file with text.  type nul > file.txt  creates an empty file.
example:
type nul > empty.txt
echo hello > hello.txt
notepad new.txt

title: Folder tree
desc: Shows the folder structure as a tree (with /f, also files).

title: Search for files by name
desc: Searches the current folder and subfolders.

title: Search text inside files
desc: Searches for text inside files in this folder and subfolders. /n shows line numbers.

title: Compare two files
desc: Shows the differences between two files. /b for binary compare.
example:
fc old.txt new.txt
fc /b a.exe b.exe

title: Hide / unhide a file or folder (attrib)
desc: +h hidden, +s system, +r read-only. Use - to remove.

title: Show hidden files from a virus-infected USB
desc: Some USB viruses hide all your files and leave shortcuts. Replace E: with your USB drive letter. Then delete the .lnk shortcuts and scan with antivirus.

title: File checksum / hash
desc: Calculates a file's hash to verify downloads. Also MD5, SHA1.
example:
certutil -hashfile setup.iso SHA256
certutil -hashfile file.zip MD5

title: Zip / unzip files
desc: Windows 10/11 includes tar which can make and extract zip files.
example:
tar -a -c -f backup.zip Folder
tar -xf backup.zip
tar -xf backup.zip -C D:\Out

title: Take ownership of a file/folder
desc: Makes you the owner (fixes 'Access is denied' on files). Then grant full rights with icacls.

title: Change permissions (icacls)
desc: Shows or changes file permissions. F = full, M = modify, R = read. /t = subfolders. /reset resets to inherited.

title: Create a shortcut link (mklink)
desc: Creates a symbolic link. /d for folder, /j junction. Useful to move a big folder to another drive and keep the path working.

title: Folder size
desc: The last lines show the total size. For a nicer view use PowerShell.
example:
dir /s "C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Downloads" | findstr "File(s)"
powershell "(gci -r C:\Data | measure Length -s).Sum/1GB"

title: Open Explorer at current folder
desc: Opens the current folder in File Explorer.  explorer <path>  opens any folder.

title: Encrypt / compress a folder
desc: NTFS-compresses files to save disk space. cipher /e encrypts (Pro editions).

title: Check and repair disk errors (chkdsk)
desc: Scans the disk for errors. /f fixes errors, /r finds bad sectors (slow). For C: it asks to run at next restart - type Y and reboot.
example:
chkdsk C:          :: just check (read-only)
chkdsk D: /f
chkdsk C: /f /r /x

title: Manage partitions (diskpart)
desc:
Powerful disk tool. Inside diskpart:
  list disk
  select disk 1
  list partition / list volume
  exit
Be VERY careful selecting the right disk.

title: Format / repair a USB that shows wrong size or won't format
desc:
In diskpart (ALL DATA on that disk is erased!):
  list disk
  select disk X        (X = your USB, check the size!)
  clean
  create partition primary
  format fs=fat32 quick     (or fs=ntfs / exfat)
  assign
  exit

title: Remove write protection from a USB
desc:
In diskpart:
  list disk
  select disk X
  attributes disk clear readonly
  exit
If it still fails, the USB may have a physical lock switch or be dying.

title: Format a drive
desc: Formats a drive. /q quick format. /fs: ntfs, fat32, exfat. ERASES ALL DATA.

title: Free space on drives
desc: Shows free space (bytes) on all drives. PowerShell version is nicer.
example:
powershell "Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem"
fsutil volume diskfree C:

title: Clean temporary files
desc: Deletes your temporary files (some in use will be skipped - that's normal). Also run  cleanmgr  for Disk Cleanup.

title: Disk Cleanup (including system files)
desc: Opens Disk Cleanup. Click 'Clean up system files' to remove old Windows Update files.

title: Clean old Windows Update leftovers (WinSxS)
desc: Frees space used by old updates in C:\Windows\WinSxS. /ResetBase frees more but you can't uninstall updates after.

title: Disable hibernation (frees GBs on C:)
desc: Deletes hiberfil.sys (often several GB). Disables hibernate and Fast Startup. powercfg /h on to re-enable.

title: Defragment / optimize drive
desc: Optimizes the drive (defrag for HDD, TRIM for SSD). /a = analyze only.

title: Disk health (SMART status)
desc: 'OK' means SMART sees no problem. 'Pred Fail' = back up NOW, disk is dying.

title: Change drive letter
desc:
In diskpart:
  list volume
  select volume N
  assign letter=Z
  exit
Or: Win+R > diskmgmt.msc

title: Convert drive FAT32 to NTFS (no data loss)
desc: Converts without erasing. Fixes 'file is too large for the destination file system' (FAT32 4GB limit).

title: Disk Management window
desc: Opens the graphical Disk Management tool.

title: Show IP address and network info
desc: Shows your IP, gateway (router) and subnet. /all shows MAC address, DNS servers, DHCP.

title: Fix internet: release / renew IP
desc: Asks the router for a new IP address. Fixes 'No Internet' / 'Limited connectivity' / 169.254.x.x addresses.

title: Flush DNS cache
desc: Clears saved DNS. Fixes sites not loading, wrong sites, DNS_PROBE_FINISHED errors after DNS change.

title: FULL network reset (fixes most internet problems)
cmd:
netsh winsock reset
netsh int ip reset
ipconfig /release
ipconfig /renew
ipconfig /flushdns
desc:
Resets Winsock catalog and TCP/IP stack to default. Restart the PC after. Fixes many 'No internet' issues, broken connections after VPN/malware removal.
Also: Settings > Network > Advanced > Network reset.

title: Ping (test connection)
desc:
Tests if a host answers and shows delay (ms). -t = continuous (Ctrl+C to stop). -n 10 = 10 times.
ping 8.8.8.8 works but ping google.com doesn't = DNS problem.
example:
ping 8.8.8.8
ping google.com -t
ping 192.168.1.1     :: your router

title: Trace route (where the connection breaks)
desc: Shows every hop between you and the server. Where it starts timing out is where the problem is. pathping is a slower, more detailed version.

title: DNS lookup
desc: Shows which IP a domain points to, and which DNS server answered.
example:
nslookup google.com 8.8.8.8     :: ask Google DNS
nslookup -type=mx gmail.com

title: Show open connections & ports
desc: -a all, -n numeric, -o process ID (PID). Find PID then check it with tasklist.
example:
netstat -ano | findstr LISTENING
netstat -ano | findstr :3000
tasklist /fi "PID eq 1234"
netstat -b      :: show program names (admin)

title: Port already in use - find and kill it
desc:
Find the PID using the port (last column) then kill it:
  taskkill /PID <pid> /F
Fixes 'Address already in use', 'EADDRINUSE', 'port 8080 is already in use'.

title: Show saved Wi-Fi networks
desc: Lists all Wi-Fi networks saved on this PC.

title: Show saved Wi-Fi password
cmd: netsh wlan show profile name="<WiFi name>" key=clear
desc: Shows the password of a Wi-Fi network this PC has connected to before (look for 'Key Content').
example: netsh wlan show profile name="MyHome" key=clear | findstr Key

title: Forget a Wi-Fi network
cmd: netsh wlan delete profile name="<WiFi name>"
desc: Deletes a saved Wi-Fi network (fixes wrong saved password).

title: Wi-Fi adapter info / signal
desc: Shows current Wi-Fi network, signal %, speed, channel.

title: Wi-Fi report (why Wi-Fi disconnects)
desc: Generates an HTML report of Wi-Fi sessions & disconnections in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WlanReport\.

title: Change DNS to Google / Cloudflare
cmd: netsh interface ip set dns name="Wi-Fi" static 8.8.8.8
desc: Sets DNS server for an adapter. Use your adapter name from  netsh interface show interface  ("Wi-Fi" or "Ethernet").
example:
netsh interface ip set dns name="Wi-Fi" static 1.1.1.1
netsh interface ip add dns name="Wi-Fi" 8.8.4.4 index=2
netsh interface ip set dns name="Wi-Fi" dhcp      :: back to automatic

title: List network adapters
desc: Shows adapters and if they're enabled/connected.
example:
netsh interface set interface "Wi-Fi" disable
netsh interface set interface "Wi-Fi" enable

title: Restart network adapter
cmd: netsh interface set interface "Wi-Fi" disable & netsh interface set interface "Wi-Fi" enable
desc: Turns the adapter off and on again. Replace "Wi-Fi" with "Ethernet" if wired.

title: Set static IP
cmd: netsh interface ip set address name="Ethernet" static 192.168.1.50 255.255.255.0 192.168.1.1
desc: Sets a fixed IP, mask and gateway. Back to automatic:  netsh interface ip set address name="Ethernet" dhcp

title: ARP table (devices on your network)
desc: Lists IP and MAC addresses of devices your PC talked to on the local network.

title: Routing table
desc: Shows the routing table.

title: Download a file from CMD
desc: Windows 10/11 include curl.
example:
curl -L -o setup.exe https://example.com/setup.exe
curl ifconfig.me          :: your public IP

title: Show public (external) IP
desc: Shows your public internet IP address.

title: Test if a port is open on a server
desc: Checks if you can reach a specific port (TcpTestSucceeded: True).

title: Firewall on / off / status
desc: Shows firewall state. Turning it off is NOT recommended except for short testing.
example:
netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off
netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state on
netsh advfirewall reset      :: back to defaults

title: Allow a port through the firewall
cmd: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="My Port 8080" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=8080
desc: Opens a port for incoming connections (servers, games). Delete with: netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name="My Port 8080"

title: Block a program in the firewall
cmd: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Block App" dir=out action=block program="C:\path\app.exe"
desc: Blocks a program from accessing the internet.

title: Share a folder on the network
desc: Shares a folder. net share alone lists shares. net share MyShare /delete removes it.

title: Connect a network drive
desc: Maps a shared folder to a drive letter. net use shows mapped drives, net use Z: /delete removes it.

title: Turn PC into a Wi-Fi hotspot
desc:
Modern way: Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile hotspot.
Old netsh hostednetwork commands don't work on most new Wi-Fi drivers. Check support with: netsh wlan show drivers  (look for 'Hosted network supported').

title: Remote Desktop to another PC
desc: Opens Remote Desktop connection.

title: Network connections window
desc: Opens Network Connections (adapter settings).

title: Hosts file (block / redirect sites)
desc: Edit as admin. Add lines like  0.0.0.0 badsite.com  to block a site. Then ipconfig /flushdns.

title: Full system information
desc: Windows version, install date, RAM, BIOS, uptime, hotfixes...
example:
systeminfo | findstr /c:"OS Name" /c:"OS Version" /c:"Total Physical Memory"
systeminfo > C:\sysinfo.txt

title: Windows version
desc: Shows the Windows version window.  ver  prints it in CMD.

title: Computer name
desc: Shows the PC name.

title: CPU info
desc: Processor model, cores and threads.

title: RAM info (size, speed, slots)
desc: Shows each RAM stick.

title: GPU / graphics card info
desc: Shows graphics card and driver version. dxdiag gives a full report.

title: Motherboard & BIOS info
cmd:
wmic baseboard get product,manufacturer
wmic bios get smbiosbiosversion,serialnumber
desc: Motherboard model and BIOS version.

title: Serial number of the PC / laptop
desc: Shows the device serial number (for warranty).

title: Windows product key (from BIOS)
desc: Shows the key embedded in BIOS on laptops/PCs that came with Windows. Empty = no OEM key.

title: Check Windows activation
desc: Shows if Windows is activated. slmgr /dli = license info, slmgr /dlv = detailed.

title: Battery health report (laptop)
desc: Creates battery-report.html in the current folder. Compare DESIGN CAPACITY vs FULL CHARGE CAPACITY to see battery wear.

title: Uptime (how long since restart)
desc: Shows when the PC last booted.

title: Installed programs list
desc: Lists installed programs (winget is included in Windows 10/11).
example:
wmic product get name,version    :: slow, only MSI
winget list > programs.txt

title: DirectX diagnostics
desc: Opens DirectX diagnostic tool (graphics, sound, drivers). /t saves to a file.

title: Installed drivers list
desc: Lists drivers. /v verbose, /si signed info.

title: Installed updates (hotfixes)
desc: Lists installed Windows updates (KB numbers).

title: System Information window
desc: Detailed GUI with all hardware and software info.

title: Energy / power efficiency report
desc: Analyzes power problems for 60 sec and creates energy-report.html.

title: What wakes up my PC from sleep
desc: Shows what woke the PC.  powercfg /waketimers  shows scheduled wakes.  powercfg /devicequery wake_armed  shows devices allowed to wake.

title: List running programs (tasklist)
desc: Shows running processes with PID and memory.
example:
tasklist | findstr /i chrome
tasklist /fi "memusage gt 500000"   :: using > 500MB
tasklist /svc

title: Kill a program that is not responding
desc: Force-closes a program by name or by PID. /t also kills child processes.
example:
taskkill /im chrome.exe /f
taskkill /pid 1234 /f
taskkill /f /fi "status eq not responding"

title: Restart Windows Explorer (taskbar frozen)
desc: Fixes frozen taskbar, desktop or Start menu without restarting the PC.

title: Open Task Manager
desc: Opens Task Manager (or Ctrl+Shift+Esc).

title: List services
desc: Lists running services. sc query state= all shows all. net start lists started services.
example:
sc query state= all | findstr SERVICE_NAME
net start

title: Start / stop / restart a service
desc: Stops and starts a Windows service.
example:
net stop spooler && net start spooler
sc stop wuauserv
sc start wuauserv

title: Disable / enable a service
desc: start= auto | demand (manual) | disabled. Note the space after =.
example:
sc config SysMain start= disabled
sc config SysMain start= auto

title: Services window
desc: Opens the Services manager.

title: Startup programs
desc: Lists programs that start with Windows. Manage them in Task Manager > Startup, or open the startup folder with  start shell:startup

title: Schedule a task
desc: Runs a program on a schedule. /sc: once, daily, weekly, onlogon, onstart.
example:
schtasks /create /tn "Backup" /tr "C:\backup.bat" /sc daily /st 22:00
schtasks /query /fo list | more
schtasks /delete /tn "Backup" /f
schtasks /run /tn "Backup"

title: Run a program as another user
desc: Starts a program under another account.

title: Set process priority
cmd: wmic process where name="game.exe" CALL setpriority "high priority"
desc: Changes priority: idle, below normal, normal, above normal, high priority, realtime.

title: List user accounts
desc: Lists all local accounts. net user <name> shows details.

title: Create a new user
desc: Creates a local account.

title: Make a user Administrator
desc: Adds a user to the Administrators group. Use /delete to remove.

title: Change / reset a user's password
desc: Sets a new password.  net user <name> *  asks for it hidden.

title: Delete a user
desc: Deletes a local account (its files in C:\Users stay).

title: Enable the hidden Administrator account
desc: Enables the built-in Administrator. Set a password! /active:no to disable again.

title: Local users & groups window
desc: GUI to manage users and groups (Pro editions). Or:  netplwiz

title: Lock / sign out / switch user
desc: Locks the PC (same as Win+L).  logoff  or  shutdown /l  signs out.

title: Shut down
desc: Shuts down now. /t = seconds delay.

title: Restart
desc: Restarts the PC now.

title: Schedule shutdown & cancel it
desc: Shutdown timer. shutdown /a cancels it.

title: Restart into BIOS / UEFI
desc: Reboots directly into the BIOS/UEFI settings (UEFI PCs only).

title: Restart into Advanced Startup (recovery options)
desc: Opens the blue recovery menu: Safe Mode, Startup Repair, System Restore, Command Prompt, uninstall updates.

title: Boot into Safe Mode
desc:
Next restart boots in Safe Mode. Use 'network' instead of 'minimal' for networking.
IMPORTANT: undo afterwards with:  bcdedit /deletevalue {current} safeboot

title: Exit Safe Mode (stuck in Safe Mode)
desc: Removes the Safe Mode flag so Windows boots normally.

title: Sleep / hibernate
desc: Puts the PC to sleep (if hibernation is on it hibernates instead).  shutdown /h  hibernates.

title: Power plans
desc: Lists power plans. Switch with /setactive.
example:
powercfg /setactive SCHEME_MIN      :: High performance
powercfg /setactive SCHEME_BALANCED
powercfg -duplicatescheme e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61   :: Ultimate Performance

title: Turn off screen timeout / sleep
desc: 0 = never. Also monitor-timeout-ac, -dc for battery.

title: Repair Windows system files (SFC)
desc: Scans and repairs corrupted Windows files. Takes 10-20 min. If it says it couldn't fix some files, run DISM first then sfc again.

title: Repair the Windows image (DISM) - run before SFC
desc:
Downloads good copies of Windows files from Windows Update and repairs the system image. Then sfc fixes the files. Best general repair combo.
Check only: /CheckHealth or /ScanHealth.

title: DISM error 0x800f081f (source files not found)
desc: DISM can't download files. Mount a Windows ISO (double-click it), note its drive letter (D: here). If the ISO has install.esd instead, use esd: instead of wim:.
tags: source files could not be found

title: System Restore
desc: Opens System Restore to roll back Windows to an earlier restore point.

title: Create a restore point
cmd: wmic.exe /Namespace:\\root\default Path SystemRestore Call CreateRestorePoint "Before changes", 100, 7
desc: Creates a restore point now (System Protection must be on).

title: Fix boot: Startup / boot repair (bootrec)
desc:
Run from the recovery Command Prompt (boot from Windows USB > Repair your computer > Troubleshoot > Command Prompt).
Fixes 'BOOTMGR is missing', 'Operating System not found', boot loops.
If /fixboot says Access is denied, see the UEFI entry.

title: Fix boot on UEFI/GPT PCs (bcdboot)
cmd:
diskpart
:: list vol  ->  find the FAT32 ~100MB EFI volume
:: select vol N
:: assign letter=S
:: exit
bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI
desc: Rebuilds the boot files on the EFI partition. Run from recovery Command Prompt. C: must be the Windows drive (check with  dir C:\ ; in recovery it may be D:).

title: Check disk from recovery (Windows won't boot)
desc: In recovery Command Prompt, letters can change - find Windows with  dir C:\  dir D:\ ...

title: Run SFC offline (from recovery)
desc: Repairs system files when Windows doesn't boot. Adjust C: to the Windows drive.

title: Reset Windows (keep or remove files)
desc: Opens 'Reset this PC'. You can keep personal files. Cloud download reinstalls a fresh Windows.

title: Re-register Windows Store apps (Start menu / apps broken)
desc: Re-registers built-in apps. Fixes Start menu, Settings, Calculator or Store apps not opening. Errors in red for some apps are normal.

title: Reset Microsoft Store
desc: Clears the Store cache. Fixes Store not loading / downloads stuck.

title: Rebuild icon cache (wrong / blank icons)
cmd:
ie4uinit.exe -show
taskkill /f /im explorer.exe
del /a /q %localappdata%\IconCache.db
del /a /f /q %localappdata%\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer\iconcache*
start explorer.exe
desc: Fixes white/blank/wrong icons on desktop and Explorer.

title: Fix printer stuck queue (Print Spooler)
cmd:
net stop spooler
del /q /f /s %systemroot%\System32\spool\PRINTERS\*
net start spooler
desc: Clears stuck print jobs and restarts the spooler. Fixes 'printer offline' / jobs stuck / can't delete document.

title: Windows Memory Diagnostic (test RAM)
desc: Restarts and tests your RAM. Good for random blue screens and crashes.

title: Device Manager
desc: Opens Device Manager - yellow ! = driver problem. Right-click > Update / Uninstall driver.

title: Rescan / reinstall devices
desc: Scans for hardware changes (like Device Manager > Scan). pnputil /enum-devices /problem lists devices with problems.

title: Event Viewer (see why something crashed)
desc: Windows Logs > System / Application. Look for red Errors at the time of the problem.
example: wevtutil qe System /c:20 /rd:true /f:text /q:"*[System[(Level=1 or Level=2)]]"   :: last 20 errors

title: Reliability Monitor (crash history)
desc: Easy timeline of crashes, failed updates and errors.

title: Group Policy reset
desc: Resets local group policies to default (fixes 'Some settings are managed by your organization' on home PCs).

title: Update group policy
desc: Applies group policy changes now.

title: Reset Windows Update (stuck / failing updates)
cmd:
net stop wuauserv
net stop cryptSvc
net stop bits
net stop msiserver
ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old
ren C:\Windows\System32\catroot2 catroot2.old
net start wuauserv
net start cryptSvc
net start bits
net start msiserver
desc: Resets the update cache. Fixes updates stuck at 0% / downloading forever, and most errors like 0x80070002, 0x8024a105, 0x80073712, 0x800f0922. Restart and try updating again.

title: Check for updates from CMD
desc: Opens a check for updates. Or: start ms-settings:windowsupdate

title: Uninstall a bad update
desc: Removes an update that caused problems. Find the KB number with  wmic qfe list brief.

title: Update all programs at once (winget)
desc: Updates all apps that winget knows. winget upgrade shows what's available.

title: Install a program from CMD (winget)

example:

title: 'xxx' is not recognized as an internal or external command
desc:
CMD can't find the program.
1. Check spelling.
2. The program isn't installed, or its folder isn't in PATH. Run  where <name>  - if nothing is found, add the program's folder to PATH (see 'Add a folder to PATH') and open a NEW CMD window.
3. For python/node/git: reinstall and tick 'Add to PATH'.
4. Some tools must be run from their own folder: cd into it first.

title: Access is denied
desc:
1. Run CMD as Administrator (Win+R, cmd, Ctrl+Shift+Enter).
2. File in use: close the program using it (or restart).
3. File owned by another user: take ownership:
     takeown /f "<path>" /r /d y
     icacls "<path>" /grant %USERNAME%:F /t
4. Antivirus may be blocking it.
5. File is read-only:  attrib -r "<path>"

title: The system cannot find the path specified / file specified
desc:
The folder or file doesn't exist where you said.
- Paths with spaces MUST be in quotes: cd "C:\Program Files"
- Check the drive letter and spelling with  dir
- Use  cd /d  when changing to another drive.

title: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process
desc:
Another program has the file open.
1. Close programs that might use it (Word, Explorer preview pane, game launcher...).
2. Find the program: Resource Monitor (resmon) > CPU > 'Associated Handles' > search the file name.
3. Kill it with taskkill /im <name> /f, or restart the PC.

title: File / folder name too long (can't delete or copy)
desc:
Trick: create an empty folder C:\Empty, then mirror it onto the long folder with robocopy /purge which deletes everything inside, then delete the folder.
To allow long paths permanently (Windows 10+):
  reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem /v LongPathsEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f

title: Can't delete a file / folder (stubborn)
desc:
1. Close programs, restart Explorer.
2. Take ownership (takeown + icacls).
3. Use \\?\ prefix for weird names (ending with space or dot).
4. Delete in Safe Mode.
5. Run chkdsk if Windows says the file is corrupted.

title: No internet / 'Connected, no internet' / limited
cmd:
netsh winsock reset
netsh int ip reset
ipconfig /release
ipconfig /renew
ipconfig /flushdns
desc:
Step by step:
1. Restart router and PC.
2. ping 192.168.1.1 (router) - fails = problem between PC and router (cable/Wi-Fi/driver).
3. ping 8.8.8.8 - fails = router/ISP has no internet.
4. ping google.com fails but 8.8.8.8 works = DNS problem -> change DNS to 8.8.8.8 and flushdns.
5. Run the reset commands (as admin), restart.
6. Update/reinstall network driver in Device Manager.
7. Disable VPN / proxy (inetcpl.cpl > Connections > LAN settings).

title: DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN / DNS server not responding
cmd:
ipconfig /flushdns
netsh interface ip set dns name="Wi-Fi" static 8.8.8.8
ipconfig /registerdns
desc: The DNS can't find the site. Flush DNS and switch to Google (8.8.8.8) or Cloudflare (1.1.1.1). Replace "Wi-Fi" with "Ethernet" if wired. Also restart the 'DNS Client' service by rebooting.

title: IP address starts with 169.254 (APIPA)
desc: The PC didn't get an IP from the router (DHCP). Restart the router, check cable/Wi-Fi password, run release/renew, then the full network reset.

title: Blue Screen (BSOD) - find the cause
desc:
1. Note the STOP CODE on the blue screen (e.g. IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL, MEMORY_MANAGEMENT, CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED) and search it here.
2. Event Viewer > System > 'BugCheck' events.
3. Dump files are in C:\Windows\Minidump (open with WinDbg or BlueScreenView).
4. General fixes: update drivers (GPU, chipset, Wi-Fi), run  sfc /scannow  + DISM, test RAM (mdsched), chkdsk, uninstall recently installed programs/updates, check overheating.

title: BSOD: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT / PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA
desc: Usually RAM or driver problem. Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (mdsched), reseat RAM sticks, disable XMP/overclock in BIOS, update drivers, run sfc /scannow.

title: BSOD: IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL / DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
desc: A driver is misbehaving. The blue screen may name a .sys file - search it to find the driver (e.g. nvlddmkm.sys = NVIDIA, rt640x64.sys = Realtek LAN). Update or roll back that driver. Also check RAM.

title: BSOD: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED / SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION
desc: Often corrupted system files, bad driver or failing disk. Run DISM + SFC + chkdsk, update drivers, uninstall recent updates.

title: BSOD: INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE
desc:
Windows can't read its boot disk.
1. In BIOS check SATA mode (AHCI vs RAID/IDE) - change it back if you changed it.
2. Boot recovery > Uninstall latest update.
3. Recovery Command Prompt: chkdsk C: /f, then bootrec / bcdboot commands.
4. Check disk cables / disk health.

title: BSOD: VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE / screen goes black then recovers
desc: Graphics driver crash. Clean-reinstall the GPU driver (use DDU in Safe Mode), remove GPU overclock, check GPU temperature and power cables.

title: Automatic Repair loop / 'Your PC did not start correctly'
desc:
Advanced options > Command Prompt. Find your Windows drive (dir C:\, dir D:\). Run chkdsk, offline sfc, boot repair. Or Advanced options > Uninstall Updates / System Restore.
To disable the auto-repair loop:  bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled no

title: BOOTMGR is missing / Operating system not found
desc:
1. Remove USB sticks / DVDs and check BIOS boot order.
2. Boot from a Windows USB > Repair your computer > Command Prompt and run the commands.
3. On UEFI PCs use bcdboot (see 'Fix boot on UEFI').

title: Windows Update error 0x80070002 / 0x80070003 / 0x8024xxxx
cmd:
net stop wuauserv
net stop bits
ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old
net start wuauserv
net start bits
desc: Corrupted update cache. Reset it (see 'Reset Windows Update'), then run DISM + sfc, check date/time is correct, and free up disk space (at least 20 GB).

title: Windows Update error 0x800f0922 / 0x800f081f / 0x80073712
desc: Component store is damaged or System Reserved partition is full. Run DISM + SFC, disable VPN, make sure .NET Framework is enabled, then retry. Use the Windows Update Assistant / Media Creation Tool to do an in-place upgrade if it still fails (keeps files & apps).

title: Error 0xc000007b - application was unable to start correctly
desc: Missing/mixed 32/64-bit DLLs. Install/repair all Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables (x86 AND x64), DirectX End-User Runtime and .NET Framework, then reinstall the program.
example:
winget install Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64
winget install Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x86

title: MSVCP140.dll / VCRUNTIME140.dll / xxx.dll is missing
cmd:
winget install Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64
winget install Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x86
desc: Install the Visual C++ Redistributable (both x64 and x86). For d3dx9_xx.dll install DirectX End-User Runtime. Never download single DLLs from random sites.

title: Error 0x80070005 (access denied in installers/updates)
desc: Permissions problem. Run the installer as Administrator, temporarily disable antivirus, make sure the account is admin, and check date/time. For update errors reset Windows Update.

title: 'Windows protected your PC' (SmartScreen)
desc: Windows blocks unknown programs. If you trust the file: click 'More info' > 'Run anyway'. Or right-click file > Properties > tick 'Unblock'. Only do this for files you trust!

title: 'This app can't run on your PC'
desc: Usually a 32/64-bit or ARM mismatch, or the file is corrupt/incomplete. Download the correct version for your system (check: systeminfo | findstr Type), re-download the file.
tags: this app can't run on your pc

title: PowerShell: running scripts is disabled on this system
desc: Allows running local .ps1 scripts for your user. Or run one script with: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File script.ps1

title: Not enough disk space / C: drive full
desc:
1. Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files.
2. del /s /q %TEMP%\*
3. powercfg /h off (removes hiberfil.sys)
4. DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup
5. Empty Recycle Bin, Downloads.
6. Find big folders: Settings > System > Storage.

title: PC is very slow
desc:
1. Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) - sort by CPU / Memory / Disk to see what's using it.
2. Disable startup apps (Task Manager > Startup).
3. Check disk space, scan for viruses.
4. sfc /scannow + DISM.
5. If Disk is at 100% on an HDD - consider an SSD.
6. Check disk health: wmic diskdrive get status

title: 100% disk usage
cmd:
sc stop SysMain
sc config SysMain start= disabled
desc: Common on HDDs. Try: disable SysMain (Superfetch), disable Windows Search indexing temporarily (sc stop WSearch), check for updates running, scan disk health. Real fix: upgrade to SSD.

title: High CPU from 'Antimalware Service Executable'
desc:
Windows Defender is scanning. Let it finish, or schedule scans. Adding exclusions for big game/dev folders helps:
  powershell Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "D:\Games"

title: No sound
cmd: net stop audiosrv && net start audiosrv
desc:
1. Check the right output device (click speaker icon) and volume mixer.
2. Restart the audio service (command above, as admin).
3. mmsys.cpl > set default device.
4. Device Manager > Sound > uninstall driver > restart.
5. Settings > Sound > Troubleshoot.

title: USB device not recognized
desc: Try another port/cable, restart PC, Device Manager > Universal Serial Bus controllers > uninstall 'Unknown USB Device' and rescan. Disable USB selective suspend in Power Options.

title: USB / drive shows as RAW or asks to format
desc: Don't format if you need the data! Run chkdsk on it first. If that fails, use recovery software (e.g. TestDisk/PhotoRec) BEFORE formatting.
tags: you need to format the disk

title: Start menu / taskbar / search not working
desc:
1. Restart Explorer (command above).
2. sfc /scannow + DISM.
3. Re-register apps (see 'Re-register Windows Store apps').
4. Create a new user account to test.

title: Keyboard / mouse not working
desc: Try another USB port, check batteries/Bluetooth pairing, Device Manager > uninstall device > restart. For keyboard: Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard - make sure Filter Keys is OFF. Use 'osk' (On-Screen Keyboard) meanwhile.

title: Bluetooth not working / missing
cmd: net stop bthserv && net start bthserv
desc: Restart Bluetooth service, toggle Airplane mode, Device Manager > Bluetooth > update/uninstall driver, run Settings > Troubleshoot > Bluetooth.

title: Time / date always wrong
desc: Syncs the clock with the internet. If it's wrong after every shutdown, the CMOS battery on the motherboard is dead.

title: 'Your organization manages some settings' / settings greyed out
desc: On a home PC this is often left by tweaking tools. See 'Group Policy reset' in Windows Repair.

title: Windows not activated / activation error
desc:
Check status with slmgr /dli. If you have a valid key:  slmgr /ipk <key>  then  slmgr /ato. If the PC came with Windows, get the BIOS key:  wmic path softwarelicensingservice get OA3xOriginalProductKey.
Also: Settings > Activation > Troubleshoot.

title: Program won't uninstall
desc: Try winget uninstall, appwiz.cpl, or Microsoft's 'Program Install and Uninstall troubleshooter'. As last resort delete its folder and registry leftovers.

title: Batch script closes immediately
desc: Run it from an open CMD window to see the error, or add  pause  at the end of the .bat file. Check for paths with spaces (use quotes) and use  cd /d "%~dp0"  at the top to run from the script's folder.

title: Arabic / special characters show as ??? in CMD
desc: Switch to UTF-8, and change the CMD font to one that supports Arabic (right-click title bar > Properties > Font). Windows Terminal displays Arabic better.

title: 'The requested operation requires elevation' (error 740)
desc: The command needs Administrator rights. Open CMD as admin (Win+R, cmd, Ctrl+Shift+Enter), or use the 'Run as Admin' button in this program.

title: 'Windows cannot access \\computer' (network share)
desc: Check both PCs are on the same network set to Private, Network discovery and File sharing are ON (control /name Microsoft.NetworkAndSharingCenter > Advanced sharing settings), and the user has permission. Use  \\IP\share  instead of name.

title: Error 0x80070035 - The network path was not found
cmd:
sc config lanmanworkstation start= auto
net start lanmanworkstation
desc: Enable Network discovery & File sharing, make sure the 'Workstation' and 'Server' services are running, and try the IP address instead of the computer name.

title: Game / program crashes on start
desc: Update GPU drivers, install VC++ Redistributables + DirectX, verify game files in Steam/Epic, run as admin, add exception in antivirus, check Event Viewer > Application for the crash module name.

title: Screen black after login (only cursor)
desc: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc > File > Run new task > type  explorer.exe . If it works, run sfc /scannow and check for malware. Win+Ctrl+Shift+B restarts the graphics driver.

title: Forgot Windows password (local account)
desc:
Microsoft account: reset at account.live.com/password/reset.
Local account on your own PC: if another admin account exists, log in there and run:  net user <name> <newpassword>
Otherwise use the security questions on the login screen or a password-reset disk.

title: Basic .bat script template
cmd:
@echo off
title My Script
cd /d "%~dp0"
echo Hello %USERNAME%
pause
desc: Save in Notepad as  script.bat  (Save as type: All files). @echo off hides commands, %~dp0 = folder of the script.

title: Variables in batch
cmd:
set name=Ali
echo Hello %name%
set /a sum=5+3
set /p answer=Type something:
desc: set = text, set /a = math, set /p = ask the user for input.

title: IF conditions
desc: Comparisons: == equ neq lss leq gtr geq. /i ignores case.

title: FOR loops
cmd:
for %%f in (*.txt) do echo %%f
for /l %%i in (1,1,10) do echo %%i
for /r %%f in (*.jpg) do echo %%f
for /f "tokens=*" %%l in (list.txt) do echo %%l
desc: In a .bat use %%f, directly in CMD use %f. /l = numbers, /r = recursive, /f = read file/command output.

title: Labels and GOTO / menus
cmd:
:menu
cls
echo 1. Ping Google
echo 2. Exit
set /p c=Choose: 
if "%c%"=="1" ping google.com & pause & goto menu
if "%c%"=="2" exit
desc: Make simple menus with labels and goto. choice  is another way: choice /c 12 /m "Choose"

title: Run a batch script as admin automatically
desc: Put this at the top of a .bat - it restarts itself as Administrator if needed.

title: Call another script / functions
cmd:
call other.bat
call :myfunc arg1
exit /b
:myfunc
echo got %1
exit /b
desc: call runs another batch and comes back. %1 %2 are arguments.

title: Date-stamped backup folder
desc: Creates a folder with the date. The %date% format depends on region settings - check with echo %date%.

title: Run a PowerShell command from CMD
desc: Runs PowerShell inside CMD. Type  powershell  alone to switch shells, exit to come back.

title: Top 10 processes by memory
desc: Shows which programs use the most RAM.

title: Find biggest files on a drive
desc: Lists the 20 largest files (takes a while). Change C:\ to any folder.

title: Get Windows product key / install info
desc: Detailed Windows info.

title: Wi-Fi passwords of ALL saved networks
cmd: for /f "tokens=2 delims=:" %a in ('netsh wlan show profiles ^| findstr "All User"') do @netsh wlan show profile name=%a key=clear | findstr "SSID Key"
desc: Shows every saved Wi-Fi name and its password on this PC (paste in CMD directly, not in a .bat).
